messages:
Sam: Quick q — for the new internal API, should we do dual-stack (clients speak gRPC; external REST front) or ship a lightweight translator at the edge that converts REST->gRPC? Main concerns: quotas attribution, telemetry fidelity, and rollout UX.

Anya: Edge translator = easier for clients (no client changes) but adds another failure surface and latency. Also makes attribution trickier unless we pass through tenant headers.

Kelsey: +1 on the attribution point. Whatever we pick, we need a clear header mapping strategy. Example: `x-customer-id` -> `x-tenant-id` and propagate `x-traceparent`. Otherwise console graphs will lie.

Ravi: If we do translator, it must be transparent for tracing and quotas. We should surface a `X-Quota-Owner` header from the translator into the runtime so token/billing attribution isn't done at the gateway only. Otherwise batching at the translator will blur per-tenant token counts.

Sam: That batching bit is huge — translator might do request coalescing / batching for throughput. How do we avoid cross-tenant token charging?

Anya: Enforce tenant-aware batching. Implementation sketch: `batchKey = tenant_id + model_id` so we never mix tokens across tenants. Also store separate KV caches per tenant.

Kelsey: Console/rollout UX ask: the rollout UI should show which routes and tenants are affected by a canary and allow one-click rollback. If telemetry is aggregated incorrectly we'll get false positives and rollback the wrong thing.

Ravi: Alternative: dual-stack approach — encourage clients to speak gRPC natively (new SDKs) and only keep a thin gateway for auth/quotas for legacy REST traffic. Pros: simpler telemetry (no translation layer), clearer contracts. Cons: client migration cost.

Sam: I'm leaning dual-stack for long-term sanity, but worried about adoption curve. Could we phase: translator v1 -> dual-stack migration with console assisted rollout?

Kelsey: Yep. Console should support phased rollouts by header (e.g., `X-Use-GRPC: 1`) and by percentage. We should also show per-route token burn and per-tenant latency in the canary dashboard.

Anya: Small config example for translator header mapping:
```\nmappings:\n  inbound.headers:\n    - from: x-customer-id\n      to: X-Tenant-ID\n    - from: Authorization\n      to: Authorization\n  propagate:\n    - X-TraceParent\n    - X-Quota-Owner\n```

Ravi: And batching isolation pseudocode: `batchKey = tenant_id || ":" || model_id` — any cross-tenant merge => reject. Keep it strict.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: translator-v2 -> prod-us-east (canary id 123). <https://console.redwood/canaries/123|view canary>.

Sam: Quick thumbs: dual-stack (long-term) vs translator (short-term). Vote with emoji please.

Anya: :thumbsup: translator (with strict tenant isolation)

Ravi: :thumbsup: dual-stack (long-term)

Kelsey: :thinking_face: prefer phased approach + console improvements

Sam: Action items: 1) Sam create lightweight RFC + migration plan by EOD, 2) Kelsey mock the canary/rollback UX, 3) Ravi spike header/propagation and tenant-aware batching this week. deploy-bot: created issue #789 for the spike.

Sam: Thanks all — will send a short RFC draft and a spike checklist.
